key_insight: A foundation model that learns a ‘chemical language’ of natural products captures rich, generalizable molecular representations that power many downstream natural-product mining tasks from property prediction to generation.
problem_solved: Natural products are chemically diverse and underrepresented in existing datasets and models; this work addresses the lack of a general, pre-trained model tailored to the unique structures and patterns of natural-product chemistry.
method: Assemble a large, diverse corpus of natural-product molecular data and metadata to serve as training material.
Train a self-supervised foundation model to learn chemical 'language' representations (tokens/embeddings) that encode structure, functional motifs, and biosynthetic patterns.
Demonstrate transferability by fine-tuning or probing the model on downstream tasks relevant to natural-product mining (e.g., property prediction, annotation, retrieval, and generation).
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a reusable pretrained molecular representation specialized for natural products, reducing data requirements and improving performance on discovery, annotation, and generative tasks in natural-product research and drug discovery.

paper_title: Learning the chemical language of natural products
paper_authors: Xu Guo, Celia M. Rava, Allison S. Walker
